title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 42-49 of the 1986 'Analysis situs, troisième mouture'): Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'tame' or polyhedral topology without points. The data are a set M of 'pieces' (think closed tame subsets or cells) with an order ≤ and a stronger relation ≪ (roughly 'X' is well inside / very small relative to X'). Inside M sits a subfamily Λ of 'model' pieces (polyhedral, linear, ...). p.46 defined Λ-'spécieuse' (Λ-polyhedral) structures: Λ must be 'très dense' in M (axioms Λ1, Λ2) and M must be spécieux (axioms D, C*).

Page 47 asks a reconstruction question. Given only (M, ≤_M, ≪_M, Λ ⊂ M, ∥_Λ), where ∥_Λ is a relation on Λ (Λ assumed closed in M), what conditions guarantee that the data come from a Λ-spécieux (resp. Λ-polyhedral) situation? He treats the spécieux case.

Axioms:
- MΛ0-MΛ3: as on p.42.
- MΛ4: ∥ on Λ is symmetric and antireflexive (X∥Y ⇒ X≠Y). It is also hereditary for ≪: X∥Y, X'≪X, Y'≪Y ⇒ X'∥Y'. So ∥ is an apartness or disjointness relation ('X and Y are disjoint/separated').
- MΛ5 is a locality (gluing) axiom and replaces ML5 of p.34. Take X, Y ∈ M bounded above by a common Z, and 'shadows' X' ∈ Omb_Λ(X), Y' ∈ Omb_Λ(Y), i.e. model pieces approximating X, Y from inside. Put:
  - L = X̃ ∩ Ỹ, the common part, where X̃ is the set of pieces under X;
  - Omb(L) = ⋃_{Z∈L} Omb(Z);
  - X'_L = X̃' ∩ Omb(L), and likewise Y'_L.
  If every X'' ∈ X'_L is apart from every Y'' ∈ Y'_L (these lie in Λ since they are ≤ X', Y'), then X'∥Y'. In words: to test whether two model pieces are disjoint, it suffices to test near the common part of the ambient pieces.

Two relations are then extended from Λ to M, writing L = X̃ ∩ Ỹ:
- X ≭_M Y ⇔ for all shadows X', Y' with X'_L = ∅ = Y'_L, one has X'∥_Λ Y';
- X ∥_M Y ⇔ all shadows of X are apart from all shadows of Y.

p.48 proves:
- X ∥_M Y ⇔ (X ≭ Y and X̃ ∩ Ỹ = ∅);
- ∥_M restricts to ∥_Λ on Λ;
- ∥ extends to subsets.

The marginal 'Non, p.49' and 'cf. plus bas … vraisemblablement inutile' show he soon doubted or revised this part. The margin also says the ≭ form will be needed later in a weaker version.

Purpose: recover the global 'disjointness' (separation) structure of a tame space from the Λ-models, as a step toward an intrinsic, point-free axiomatics of polyhedral/tame spaces (the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse).
errors: MΛ5 as written quantifies over X'_L ∥ Y'_L, which is vacuously true when either X'_L or Y'_L is empty. It therefore forces X'∥Y' whenever just one of them is empty. That is geometrically reasonable (X' misses the common part, so X' ∩ Y' = ∅), but it is stronger than the ≭-definition just below, which requires both to be empty. This asymmetry is not commented on and may explain the later 'Non, p.49'.

The definitions of X̃, Omb and Omb_Λ are not restated on this page; antireflexivity of ∥_M (p.48) relies on Omb_Λ(X) ≠ ∅ via MΛ2. MΛ4's heredity uses ≪ rather than ≤, while MΛ5's NB uses X'' ≤ X'. Mixing ≤ and ≪ is consistent only if Λ is closed downward appropriately (the inserted 'partie fermée' hypothesis).
Grothendieck himself marks the construction as probably unnecessary and refers to a correction ('Non, p.49'), so it is a provisional draft rather than a settled result.

ideas.what: Axiomatizing a disjointness/apartness relation ∥ on a poset of pieces: symmetric, antireflexive, hereditary under the 'well-inside' relation ≪
ideas.modern_name: proximity / contact relation (complement of a contact relation); 'far from' relation in Efremovič proximity spaces; de Vries compingent algebras; region-based (contact-algebra) topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Efremovič (1950s), de Vries (1962), Dimov-Vakarelov, Düntsch-Winter (2000s contact algebras)

ideas.what: Locality axiom MΛ5: disjointness of approximating model pieces can be checked on shadows of the common part X̃∩Ỹ
ideas.modern_name: local character of separation / sheaf-type locality condition in point-free tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct analogue; related to o-minimal cell decomposition arguments (van den Dries) only loosely

ideas.what: Extending the relation from model pieces Λ to all of M via 'ombres' (inner Λ-approximations), with the lemma that X∥Y iff X≭Y and X̃∩Ỹ=∅
ideas.modern_name: extension of a relation along a dense sub-basis (approximation from inside, as in continuous lattices / way-below)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Scott / Gierz et al. (continuous lattices) for the general pattern

ideas.what: Overall programme: intrinsic axiomatics of Λ-polyhedral ('spécieux') structures recovering a tame topology from combinatorial order data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (programmatically, Esquisse 1984); van den Dries, Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn (o-minimality)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 states the programme but not this axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck's point-free axiomatics of tame spaces uses an order ≤, a 'well-inside' relation ≪ and a hereditary apartness ∥. This is structurally the same as de Vries algebras and contact algebras in region-based topology. That literature never drew on his 1986 'analysis situs' programme, and the o-minimal literature never adopted a contact-algebra viewpoint.
missed.quote: La relation ∥_Λ … est symétrique, antiréflexive (X∥Y ⇒ X≠Y), et X∥Y, X'≪X, Y'≪Y ⟹ X'∥Y'.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Point-free (contact-algebra / de Vries-duality) methods might give a choice-free, constructive foundation for tame or polyhedral topology, in line with Grothendieck's aims. His locality axiom MΛ5 has no obvious counterpart in contact-algebra axioms.

missed.claim: The reconstruction problem — characterizing which data (M, ≤, ≪, Λ, ∥) arise from a Λ-spécieux / Λ-polyhedral situation — is posed but left provisional (MΛ5 replaced, ≭-approach marked 'Non, p.49').
missed.quote: On voudrait donner une condition sur (M, ≤, ≪, Λ⊂M, ∥) … pour que ça provienne d'une situation Λ-spéciaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An order-theoretic characterization of definable or polyhedral structures would be a combinatorial 'reconstruction theorem' for tame topology. It is still open in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, technically specific piece of Grothendieck's late tame-topology axiomatics, and it shows a (unremarked) proximity/contact-algebra structure. But it is a provisional draft he himself partly retracted, with no finished result.
transcription_corrections: The relation in the first displayed definition is written ≭_M (as on p.48), not '#'.
Margin: 'remplace ML5 p.34' (top left), and 'On en aura besoin plus tard, sous une forme plus faible (avec X≭Y, ci-dessous)'.
Line 'Cf. plus bas … ' reads roughly 'Cf. plus bas dès que ça suffit (plus vraisemblablement inutile)'; the margin there is 'Non, p.49'.
'situation Λ-spéciaux' should read 'situation Λ-spécieuse'; 'resp. Λ-pol.' = Λ-polyédrale.
